notes: Fourth sweep (2026-10-22-c): five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) at head 3e3581d with no uncommitted changes; every run has rc 0 and a model_id matching its tier, read no skill files, and wrote blog.ex in one Write call. The Haiku runs ran only mkdir first; sonnet-2's first Bash (mkdir plus a cat heredoc) was refused by the permission check and it then used Write. No run ran elixir or mix. skills_listed is 29 in every run, against 16 in 2026-10-22-b.

Rule list: the eight rules whose index row names ecto-phoenix: the six ecto-phoenix.md rules, plus Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call and Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order. git diff 0397dec -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches only SKILL.md, references/processes.md and references/testing.md; references/ecto-phoenix.md is unchanged, so the six are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-22-b/grades/ecto-phoenix-baseline.json, including its reading that a struct of code-set values passed to Repo.insert (opus-1 line 92: {:ok, _log} <- Repo.insert(audit_log_for_publish(post))) is not the params-built struct Validate input with changesets names.

Both SKILL.md rules are new since 0397dec (added in b0bf52c, unchanged since), so this is their first verdict in a baseline sweep; they are graded against the current text to the sweeps/2026-10-22-check-7 standard. Build a multi-line argument is decided by "When an argument is a map, struct or keyword list that would span several lines, build it first under a name that says what it is, write it one field per line, and set each multi-line statement apart with a blank line." Open a module is decided by "Right after `@moduledoc`, group each kind together, in that order".

Every multi-line map, struct or keyword argument, quoted, and whether it was named first. opus-1: none passed inline; the only multi-line struct, lines 103-108 %Log{ action: ..., resource_type: ..., resource_id: ..., user_id: ... }, is the body of defp audit_log_for_publish/1, and the call takes it by that name on one line (line 92: {:ok, _log} <- Repo.insert(audit_log_for_publish(post))): named first, clean. haiku-1: lines 95-100 Log.changeset(%Log{}, %{ / action: "post.published", / resource_type: "Post", / resource_id: published.id, / user_id: published.user_id / }) inline in the Multi.insert function: not named, violated. haiku-2: lines 76-81, the same Log.changeset(%Log{}, %{ ... }) inline: not named, violated. sonnet-1: lines 111-116 Ecto.Changeset.change(%Log{}, %{ / action: "post.published", / resource: "post", / resource_id: published.id, / user_id: published.user_id / }) inline: not named, violated; also lines 83-89 Repo.all( / from p in Post, / join: ..., where: ..., order_by: ..., preload: [user: u] / ), a multi-line query passed straight into the Repo call unnamed (check-6 graded queries by whether they are named before the Repo call; this one is not piped, so it is not moved to Write pipelines). sonnet-2: lines 115-121 Log.changeset(%Log{}, %{ / action: ..., user_id: ..., resource_type: ..., resource_id: ..., / metadata: %{title: post.title, published_at: DateTime.to_iso8601(published_at)} / }) inline: not named, violated. Every run's listing and get_post! queries are one-clause-per-line pipelines (sonnet-1's listing excepted), and every controller calls render(conn, :show, post: post). Result: Opus clean, Haiku violated (2 of 2), Sonnet violated (2 of 2).

Directive order of every module (no module uses require): opus-1 MyApp.Blog.Post (no @moduledoc) use 3, import 4; MyApp.Blog @moduledoc 38-40, import 42, alias 44-47; migration use 114; controller use 137, alias 139. haiku-1 Post (no @moduledoc) use 19, import 20, alias 22; Blog (no @moduledoc) import 48, alias 50-54; migration use 115; controller use 137, alias 139. haiku-2 Post (no @moduledoc) use 5, import 6; Blog (no @moduledoc) import 35, alias 37-41; migration use 102; controller use 132, alias 134. sonnet-1 migration use 3; Post (no @moduledoc) use 23, import 24; Blog @moduledoc 56, import 58, alias 60-64; controller use 128, alias 130. sonnet-2 migration use 5; Post (no @moduledoc) use 27, import 28; Blog @moduledoc 59-61, import 63, alias 65-69; controller use 142, alias 144. All grouped, in order, first in the module body or right after @moduledoc: 5 of 5 clean. Most Post modules put use and import on adjacent lines without the blank line the rule's example shows; the rule's text does not ask for one, so that is not counted.

Keep migrations to schema changes: 5 of 5 violated, every run backfilling with execute "UPDATE posts SET published_at = inserted_at" in the column migration (opus-1 line 125, haiku-1 lines 124-127, haiku-2 line 111, sonnet-1 line 11, sonnet-2 line 13); none uses MyApp.Blog.Post, and none wrote a separate script or task. haiku-1 says so in its header, line 12: #   - No separate script is needed: the migration below does the backfill. Opus-1's comment (lines 117-119) suggests a separate batched migration for large tables, still a migration.

Validate input with changesets: both Haiku runs omit the user constraint, decided by "Declare database constraints in the changeset (`unique_constraint/3`, and `foreign_key_constraint/3` or `assoc_constraint/3` for a `belongs_to`) so a violation returns `{:error, changeset}` instead of raising." haiku-1 also casts :published_at (line 37), which publish_post/1 sets through the same changeset (line 90), against "Keep fields the code sets, such as `user_id` or `status`, out of the list passed to `cast/3`"; recorded as extra evidence, as 2026-10-22-b did for its haiku-2. Opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 use assoc_constraint(:user). Every run sets user_id on the struct.

Group writes: opus-1 uses Repo.transact/2 with a two-step with; the other four use Ecto.Multi with Repo.transaction() and normalize the error to {:error, changeset}. Opus-1 and sonnet-2 add an {:error, :already_published} clause.

other_violations follow the 2026-10-22-b standard: single-step pipes, a two-transformation pipeline on one line (2026-10-22-b flagged haiku-2's with {:ok, post} <- post |> Ecto.Changeset.change(published_at: now) |> Repo.update(); opus-1 line 91 has the same shape), and a missing @moduledoc on the context or a public context function without @doc. Missing docs on schema modules (publish_changeset/2 in opus-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2), migrations and controllers are not counted. The `do:` bodies are short pattern-matching clauses (opus-1 line 98, sonnet-2 line 130); every with has two steps; no captures; no defstruct.

format_ok: result.json reports false for all five because plain mix format adds parentheses to the Ecto and Phoenix DSL calls. As in the previous sweeps, the grader recomputed it with Code.format_string!/2 and the DSL calls (field, belongs_to, timestamps, from, add, alter, execute, remove and others) in locals_without_parens: four pass; haiku-1 fails because it leaves two blank lines between sections at lines 13-14, 42-43, 109-110, 130-131 and 146-147. Nothing compiles because Phoenix and Ecto are not installed.
